content: The document outlines the development and application of Digital Adaptation Kits (DAKs) for antenatal care (ANC) as part of a broader strategy to integrate World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines into digital health systems. The DAKs are software-neutral, standardized documentation that translates WHO guidelines into actionable formats for digital health systems. The DAK for antenatal care focuses on providing a common framework for maternal health program managers, software developers, and digital system implementers. The DAK includes eight interlinked components: health interventions and recommendations, generic personas, user scenarios, business processes and workflows, core data elements, decision-support logic, indicators and reporting requirements, and functional and non-functional requirements. These components are designed to be generic and adaptable to local contexts, enabling countries to customize them according to their specific needs. The document emphasizes the importance of digital tracking and decision-support systems in improving health outcomes. Digital tracking involves the use of electronic records to capture and store clients' health information, enabling follow-up on their health status and services received. Decision-support tools assist health workers in executing clinical protocols, scheduling services, and managing cases effectively. These systems aim to reduce lapses in care, improve accountability, and enhance the quality of health services. The DAK also addresses technical considerations for self-care interventions from the perspective of health workers promoting these interventions to clients. It highlights the need for interoperability by mapping data components to standardized terminologies, such as the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). Additionally, the DAK aligns with the broader vision of SMART Guidelines, which aim to transform guideline development and application through standards-based, machine-readable, and testable approaches. The document underscores the importance of transparency, consistency, and adherence to evidence-based recommendations in digital health systems. By providing a structured framework, the DAK facilitates the effective use of digital health investments and supports the implementation of WHO guidelines in primary health care settings.
